newsitem.title: UK: Entergy says talks with London Electricity end.
newsitem.headline: Entergy says talks with London Electricity end.

text.p: U.S. energy group Entergy said Wednesday that exploratory discussions with Britain's London Electricity Plc had taken place but "have now been discontinued."

Responding to recent newspaper speculation that the New Orleans-based company might be considering a bid for the British regional electricity company, Entergy spokesman Patrick Sweeney said the company continued to consider Britain an attractive market.
"We continue to evaluate attractive markets and investment opportunities worldwide and consider the U.K. market to be in that category," Sweeney said in a statement.

London Electricity shares rose sharply Tuesday, closing up 30-1/2 pence (51 cents) at 667 pence ($11.17), after a report in the Wall Street Journal Europe that Entergy was mulling a 1.2 billion pound ($2.0 billion) bid which would be around 700 pence ($11.73) per share.
Entergy closed Tuesday at $28.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
London Electricity had declined to comment on the report but Entergy had declined to rule it out, adding that any talks were at too early a stage to be "really meaningful."

Britain's regional electricity companies have seen a flurry of renewed bid fever in recent weeks as two of the last five remaining independents have attracted offers -- Northern Electric is fending off Omaha, Neb.-based CalEnergy, while East Midlands has agreed to a takeover by Richmond, Va.-based Dominion Resoures.
